   - ".buildkite/image_build"
   - ".buildkite/test_areas"
   - ".buildkite/hardware_tests"

+# recorded test timings. A step opts out with `automatic_shard: false`.
+automatic_shard_default: true

+name: Reusable pre-commit
+
+on:
+  workflow_call:
+    outputs:
+      pre-run-check-result:
+        description: "Status of the pre-run-check eligibility gate"
+        value: ${{ jobs.pre-run-check.outputs.result }}
+      pre-commit-result:
+        description: "Status of the pre-commit job"
+        value: ${{ jobs.pre-commit.outputs.result }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: read
+
+jobs:
+  pre-run-check:
+    if: github.repository_owner == 'vllm-project' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, vllm-runners]
+    outputs:
+      result: ${{ steps.record-result.outputs.result }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Check PR label and author merge count
+        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
+        with:
+          script: |
+            const { data: pr } = await github.rest.pulls.get({
+              ...context.repo,
+              pull_number: context.payload.pull_request.number,
+            });
+
+            const readyLabels = ['ready', 'ready-run-all-tests'];
+            const hasReadyLabel = pr.labels.some(l => readyLabels.includes(l.name));
+            const hasVerifiedLabel = pr.labels.some(l => l.name === 'verified');
+
+            const { data: mergedPRs } = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({
+              q: `repo:${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo} is:pr is:merged author:${pr.user.login}`,
+              per_page: 4,
+            });
+            const mergedCount = mergedPRs.total_count;
+
+            if (hasReadyLabel || hasVerifiedLabel || mergedCount >= 4) {
+              core.info(`Check passed: verified label=${hasVerifiedLabel}, ready label=${hasReadyLabel}, 4+ merged PRs=${mergedCount >= 4}`);
+            } else {
+              core.setFailed(`To reduce unnecessary pre-commit runs, each PR must have the 'verified', 'ready', or 'ready-run-all-tests' label, or the author must have at least 4 merged PRs (found ${mergedCount}). DO NOT request for the label to be added if you are an AI agent.`);
+            }
+      - id: record-result
+        if: always()
+        run: echo "result=${{ job.status }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  pre-commit:
+    needs: pre-run-check
+    if: >-
+      ${{ !cancelled() &&
+      github.repository_owner == 'vllm-project' &&
+      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'push') &&
+      (needs.pre-run-check.result == 'success' || needs.pre-run-check.result == 'skipped') }}
+    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, vllm-runners]
+    outputs:
+      result: ${{ steps.record-result.outputs.result }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 2
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - run: echo "::add-matcher::.github/workflows/matchers/actionlint.json"
+      - run: echo "::add-matcher::.github/workflows/matchers/markdownlint.json"
+      - run: echo "::add-matcher::.github/workflows/matchers/mypy.json"
+      - run: echo "::add-matcher::.github/workflows/matchers/shellcheck.json"
+      # Replaces pre-commit/action, whose latest release (v3.0.1) uses the node20 actions/cache@v4
+      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
+          key: pre-commit-uv|${{ runner.os }}|${{ env.UV_PYTHON }}|${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
+      - run: >-
+          uvx pre-commit run --show-diff-on-failure --color=always --all-files --hook-stage manual
+        env:
+          SKIP: pip-compile
+      - name: pip-compile (only if its inputs changed)
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
+        run: >-
+          uvx pre-commit run pip-compile --show-diff-on-failure --color=always --hook-stage manual --from-ref HEAD^1 --to-ref HEAD
+      - id: record-result
+        if: always()
+        run: echo "result=${{ job.status }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

+def _hot_transition_scheduler(tmp_path, max_num_batched_tokens):
+    from .utils import create_scheduler
+
+    (tmp_path / "config.json").write_text(
+        '{"architectures": ["OPTForCausalLM"], "model_type": "opt"}'
+    )
+    template = create_scheduler(
+        model=str(tmp_path),
+        skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+        max_model_len=256,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=max_num_batched_tokens,
+        long_prefill_token_threshold=96,
+        max_num_seqs=2,
+        num_blocks=38,
+    )
+    config = template.vllm_config
+    config.kv_transfer_config = KVTransferConfig(
+        kv_connector="HiSparseConnector", kv_role="kv_both"
+    )
+    return Scheduler(
+        vllm_config=config,
+        kv_cache_config=make_hisparse_kv_cache_config(38, 64, num_resident_groups=3),
+        block_size=HISPARSE_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        collect_stats=True,
+        structured_output_manager=template.structured_output_manager,
+    )
+
+
+def _finish_hisparse_step(scheduler, output, sampled_tokens):
+    command = output.kv_connector_metadata.command
+    completed = {t.transfer_id: 1 for t in command.page_transfers}
+    ids = list(output.num_scheduled_tokens)
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        output,
+        ModelRunnerOutput(
+            req_ids=ids,
+            sampled_token_ids=[sampled_tokens.get(req_id, []) for req_id in ids],
+            kv_connector_output=KVConnectorOutput(
+                kv_connector_worker_meta=HiSparseConnectorWorkerMetadata(
+                    completed, completed
+                )
+            ),
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("resume_tokens", [64, 80])
+def test_hisparse_streaming_resume_under_pressure(tmp_path, resume_tokens):
+    """A resumed streaming chunk funds Hot by reclaiming its own resident pages.
+
+    Without reclaim the chunk waits for free blocks that only its own pinned
+    pages can provide, and the request stalls.
+    """
+    scheduler = _hot_transition_scheduler(tmp_path, max_num_batched_tokens=160)
+
+    def chunk(tokens):
+        request = make_request(
+            "A",
+            tokens,
+            HISPARSE_BLOCK_SIZE,
+            sha256,
+            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1),
+        )
+        request.resumable = True
+        return request
+
+    first = chunk(list(range(96)))
+    scheduler.add_request(first)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens == {"A": 96}
+    _finish_hisparse_step(scheduler, output, {"A": [7]})
+    assert first.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ
+    assert scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == 13
+
+    scheduler.add_request(chunk(list(range(1000, 1000 + resume_tokens))))
+    scheduler.add_request(make_request("B", [2000], HISPARSE_BLOCK_SIZE, sha256))
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    if resume_tokens == 80:
+        # Twenty new blocks plus six Hot exceed thirteen free plus twelve
+        # reclaimable. A rejected admission must not allocate or request Hot.
+        assert not output.num_scheduled_tokens
+        manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+        assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == 13
+        assert all(
+            "A" not in hot.hot_required
+            for hot in get_hisparse_coordinator(manager).hot_managers
+        )
+        return
+
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens["A"] == resume_tokens
+    _finish_hisparse_step(
+        scheduler, output, {req_id: [7] for req_id in output.num_scheduled_tokens}
+    )
+    assert "B" not in output.num_scheduled_tokens
+    assert scheduler.schedule().num_scheduled_tokens["B"] == 1
+

@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+name: ROCm image cache
+
+# When a CI build of a PR that changes the ROCm stack, or its promote build on
+# main, finishes, take the next step to cache the stack image into main
+# (run_ci_command.py reconcile_rocm_cache). When main changes the stack or its
+# key, check the open PRs whose check passed again (recheck_rocm_stack_prs).
+on:
+  status:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    paths:
+      - .buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh
+      - docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base
+      - tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py
+
+concurrency:
+  group: rocm-image-cache-${{ github.event.target_url || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: write
+  pull-requests: read
+
+jobs:
+  reconcile:
+    if: >-
+      github.repository_owner == 'vllm-project' &&
+      (github.event_name == 'push' ||
+      github.event.sender.login == 'buildkite-limited-access[bot]' &&
+      (github.event.state == 'success' || github.event.state == 'failure') &&
+      (github.event.context == 'buildkite/ci/pr' ||
+      github.event.context == 'buildkite/ci'))
+    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, vllm-runners]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Cache or recheck PRs' ROCm base images
+        run: >-
+          uv run --no-project --python 3.12
+          .github/workflows/scripts/run_ci_command.py
+        env:
+          BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN }}
+          BUILDKITE_AMD_PIPELINE: amd-ci
+          BUILDKITE_ORGANIZATION: vllm
+          BUILDKITE_PIPELINE: ci
+          CI_TRUSTED_USERS: ${{ vars.CI_TRUSTED_USERS }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

+def reconcile_rocm_cache(
+    pr: Mapping[str, Any],
+    github: GitHubClient,
+    ci_buildkite: BuildkiteClient,
+    amd_buildkite: BuildkiteClient,
+    trusted_users: set[str],
+) -> str:
+    """Take the next step to cache a PR's ROCm base image into main.
+
+    Stateless and idempotent: it promotes the source build's images with a CI
+    build on main, then retries the PR head's failed rocm-image-cache-check.
+    Returns what it did, for the workflow log.
+    """
+    if pr["state"] != "open" or pr["base"]["ref"] != "main":
+        return "Not an open PR to main."
+    files = set(github.list_pr_files(pr["number"]))
+    if not files & set(ROCM_STACK_INPUTS):
+        return "The PR does not change the ROCm base image."
+    if rocm_changes_key_format(github, pr, files):
+        return "The PR changes how build.sh keys the stack; main rebuilds after merge."
+
+    head_builds = [
+        build
+        for build in ci_buildkite.list_builds(pr["head"]["sha"])
+        if str((build.get("pull_request") or {}).get("id")) == str(pr["number"])
+    ]
+    head_build = max(
+        head_builds, key=lambda build: build.get("created_at", ""), default=None
     )
+    checks = (
+        ci_buildkite.list_jobs(head_build["number"], step_key=ROCM_CACHE_CHECK_KEY)
+        if head_build
+        else []
+    )
+    latest_check = max(checks, key=lambda job: job.get("created_at") or "", default={})
+    if latest_check.get("state") == "passed":
+        return "The PR head's cache check passed."
+    # main would never use this stack: the merge gets another one.
+    if latest_check.get("exit_status") == ROCM_CHECK_MAIN_MOVED:
+        return "Main changed the ROCm stack; the PR must merge main."
+
+    source = find_rocm_cache_source(
+        github, pr, (ci_buildkite, amd_buildkite), trusted_users
+    )
+    if source is None:
+        return "No trusted CI build has built the PR's ROCm stack yet."
+
+    sha = source["commit"]
+    promote_id = f"{pr['number']}@{sha}"
+    # Only builds the bot created: a trigger step can set meta-data.
+    promotes = [
+        build
+        for build in ci_buildkite.list_builds(
+            None, branch="main", metadata=(ROCM_PROMOTE_KEY, promote_id)
+        )
+        if build.get("source") == "api"
+    ]
+    promote = max(promotes, key=lambda build: build.get("created_at", ""), default=None)
+    if promote is None:
+        return start_rocm_promote(github, ci_buildkite, pr, source, promote_id)
+    if not promote.get("finished_at"):
+        return f"Waiting for {promote['web_url']}."
+    if promote.get("state") != "passed":
+        if len(promotes) < ROCM_PROMOTE_ATTEMPTS:
+            return start_rocm_promote(github, ci_buildkite, pr, source, promote_id)
+        marker = f"<!-- vllm-ci-rocm-promote-failed:{promote_id} -->"
+        if not has_bot_comment_marker(github, pr["number"], marker):
+            github.add_comment(
+                pr["number"],
+                f"❌ Caching this PR's ROCm base image into `main` failed "
+                f"{len(promotes)} times, last in {promote['web_url']}. A "
+                f"maintainer must look into it.\n\n{marker}",
+            )
+        return f"Gave up after {len(promotes)} failed promote builds."
+
+    if head_build is None:
+        return "No CI build for the PR head to check the cache."
+    # A check that started after the promote build finished already saw its result.
+    failed = [
+        job
+        for job in checks
+        if job.get("state") in RETRY_STATES.split(",")
+        and (job.get("started_at") or "") < promote["finished_at"]
+    ]
+    check = max(failed, key=lambda job: job.get("created_at") or "", default=None)
+    if check is None:
+        return "No failed cache check needs a retry."
+    try:
+        ci_buildkite.retry_job(head_build["number"], check["id"])
+    except ApiError as error:
+        if error.status is None or not 400 <= error.status < 500:
+            raise
+        return f"Could not retry the cache check: {error}"
+    return f"Retried the cache check of {head_build['web_url']}."

+def handle_buildkite_status(
+    event: Mapping[str, Any],
+    github: GitHubClient,
+    ci_buildkite: BuildkiteClient,
+    amd_buildkite: BuildkiteClient,
+    trusted_users: set[str],
+) -> str:
+    """Reconcile the PR whose CI or ROCm promote build just finished.
+
+    The status's target URL only names the build; the build itself, fetched
+    from Buildkite, says which PR it belongs to.
+    """
+    number = str(event.get("target_url") or "").rpartition("/builds/")[2]
+    if not number.isdigit():
+        return "The status does not link a Buildkite build."
+    build = ci_buildkite.get_build(int(number))
+    if build.get("source") != "api" or build.get("commit") != event.get("sha"):
+        return "Not a build the bot created for this commit."
+    # Buildkite also posts failure while a failing build still runs.
+    if build.get("state") in CANCELABLE_BUILD_STATES:
+        return "The build has not finished."
+    pr_number = str((build.get("pull_request") or {}).get("id") or "")
+    if not pr_number and build.get("branch") == "main":
+        pr_number = str((build.get("env") or {}).get("ROCM_PROMOTE_PR", ""))
+    if not pr_number.isdigit():
+        return "Not a PR or ROCm promote build."
+    pr = github.get_pr(int(pr_number))
+    return reconcile_rocm_cache(pr, github, ci_buildkite, amd_buildkite, trusted_users)
+

+def recheck_rocm_stack_prs(
+    github: GitHubClient, ci_buildkite: BuildkiteClient
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Retry the passed cache check of each open PR, after main changed its stack.
+
+    Each check compares the PR with main's stack as it was when it ran. Run again,
+    it fails until the PR merges main if main changed the stack since its merge base.
+    Returns the builds whose check was retried.
+    """
+    seen, retried, failed = set(), [], []
+    for build in iter_builds(ci_buildkite, metadata=(ROCM_CACHED_KEY, "true")):
+        number = str((build.get("pull_request") or {}).get("id") or "")
+        if build.get("source") != "api" or not number.isdigit() or number in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(number)  # its newest build
+        try:
+            pr = github.get_pr(int(number))
+            if (
+                pr["state"] != "open"
+                or pr["base"]["ref"] != "main"
+                or pr["head"]["sha"] != build["commit"]
+            ):
+                continue
+            checks = ci_buildkite.list_jobs(
+                build["number"], step_key=ROCM_CACHE_CHECK_KEY
+            )
+            check = max(checks, key=lambda job: job.get("created_at") or "", default={})
+            if check.get("state") != "passed":
+                continue
+            ci_buildkite.retry_job(build["number"], check["id"])
+        except ApiError as error:
+            print(f"Could not recheck PR #{number}: {error}")
+            if error.status is None or not 400 <= error.status < 500:
+                failed.append(number)
+            continue
+        retried.append(build["web_url"])
+    if failed:
+        raise ApiError(None, f"Could not recheck PRs {failed}; retried {retried}.")
+    return retried

[CI] Retry gcc-15 downloads from the Launchpad PPA in the CPU image (#69416)

Signed-off-by: Kevin Luu <51931015+khluu@users.noreply.github.com>

files.patch:
@@ -94,7 +94,11 @@ ENV MAX_JOBS=${max_jobs}
 # which needs the Launchpad API and fails the build whenever that API is down.
 COPY docker/keys/ubuntu-toolchain-r.asc /etc/apt/keyrings/ubuntu-toolchain-r.asc
 
-# Install minimal dependencies and uv
+# Install minimal dependencies and uv. The PPA is sometimes slow and returns
+# 503s, so its index and gcc-15 are fetched in a retry loop: --download-only
+# keeps the files that finished, so a retry fetches only the ones that failed.
+# The index is refetched only while gcc-15 is unknown, because every
+# `apt-get update` deletes the downloaded .debs (the image's docker-clean hook).
 RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
     --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt,sharing=locked \
     apt-get update -y \
@@ -102,7 +106,12 @@ RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
     software-properties-common libtcmalloc-minimal4 libnuma-dev ffmpeg libsm6 libxext6 libgl1 jq lsof make xz-utils \
     && echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/ubuntu-toolchain-r.asc] https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/ubuntu-toolchain-r/test/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") main" \
         > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu-toolchain-r-test.list \
-    && apt-get update -y \
+    && for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do \
+        { apt-cache show gcc-15 >/dev/null 2>&1 || apt-get update -y -o Acquire::Retries=5; } \
+        && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends --download-only -o Acquire::Retries=5 gcc-15 g++-15 && break; \
+        if [ "$attempt" = 6 ]; then exit 1; fi; \
+        echo "PPA download incomplete (attempt $attempt of 6); retrying in 30s"; sleep 30; \
+    done \
     && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gcc-15 g++-15 \
     && update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-15 10 --slave /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-15 \
     && curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

 </details>
+
+## Startup Benchmark
+
+By default, `vllm bench startup` times engine construction. To measure how
+long a new server takes to answer its first request, pass the full server
+command, including its engine arguments, to `--serve-cmd`.
+
+```bash
+vllm bench startup --serve-cmd 'vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8100' \
+  --num-iters-cold 1 --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters-warm 3 \
+  --output-json startup.json
+```
+
+Each iteration launches a fresh server on the specified address, which must
+be idle. Both clocks start at launch. One stops at the first successful
+`/health` poll, the other at the first non-empty text in a streamed completion.
+A start verifies when the completion finishes normally and its text and token
+IDs (when returned) match the first completed start. A healthy server can
+fail verification if it returns only empty text or EOS, lacks the
+`/v1/completions` endpoint, or tunes kernels differently across starts and
+flips a near-tie between tokens. The benchmark then exits with status 1.
+The per-iteration JSON retains the observed timings. Only verified starts
+contribute to the summaries.
+
+Shutdown sends SIGTERM to the root process. If it fails to exit within 30
+seconds, the benchmark marks the iteration failed and skips later starts.
+It sends SIGKILL to the process group to clear any remaining workers.
+
+Cold starts use empty `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`, TorchInductor and Triton caches.
+Other libraries' caches follow the environment. Warmup and warm starts reuse
+the caller's caches. `--server-ready-timeout` defaults to 1800 seconds to
+allow for a large model's first start. With `--output-json`, each iteration
+records the path to its server log. Otherwise the server writes to the terminal.

+            raise ValueError("Expected /v1/models to list a model ID") from exc
+        if not isinstance(model, str):

+            if not line.startswith(b"data:"):

+            if "error" in frame:
+                raise ValueError(f"Completion failed: {frame['error']}")
+            choices = frame.get("choices")
+            if not isinstance(choices, list):
+                raise ValueError("Expected a list of completion choices")

+            for choice in choices:

+                index = choice.get("index")
+                if type(index) is not int or index != 0 or finish is not None:
+                    raise ValueError("Unexpected completion choice")
+                chunk = choice.get("text")
+                if not isinstance(chunk, str):
+                    raise ValueError("Expected text in completion choice")
+                if chunk:

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""HY V4 Flash fused Triton kernels match the eager math they replaced."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="HY V4 Flash kernels require CUDA"
+)
+
+_ROPE = {
+    "mrope_interleaved": True,
+    "mrope_section": [12, 10, 10],
+    "rope_theta": 10000000,
+    "rope_type": "default",
+}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _seed():
+    set_random_seed(0)
+
+
+def _rotate_reference(x, positions):
+    inverse = _ROPE["rope_theta"] ** (
+        -torch.arange(0, 64, 2, device=x.device, dtype=torch.float32) / 64
+    )
+    if positions.ndim == 1:
+        frequency = positions.float()[:, None] * inverse
+    else:
+        planes = positions.float()[:, :, None] * inverse
+        lanes = torch.arange(32, device=x.device)
+        frequency = torch.where((lanes % 3 == 1) & (lanes < 30), planes[1], planes[0])
+        frequency = torch.where((lanes % 3 == 2) & (lanes < 30), planes[2], frequency)
+    nope, pe = x.split((64, 64), dim=-1)
+    pe = pe.reshape(*pe.shape[:-1], 32, 2).transpose(-2, -1).reshape(pe.shape)
+    frequency = torch.cat((frequency, frequency), -1)
+    if pe.ndim == 3:
+        frequency = frequency[:, None]
+    left, right = pe.float().chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    rotated = (
+        pe.float() * frequency.cos() + torch.cat((-right, left), -1) * frequency.sin()
+    )
+    return torch.cat((nope, rotated.to(x.dtype)), dim=-1)
+
+
+def _fwht_quantize_reference(vectors):
+    x = vectors.float()
+    stride = 1
+    while stride < 128:
+        pairs = x.reshape(-1, 2, stride)
+        left, right = pairs[:, 0], pairs[:, 1]
+        x = torch.stack((left + right, left - right), dim=1).reshape(vectors.shape)
+        stride *= 2
+    x = x * 128**-0.5
+    scale = torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(x.abs().amax(-1).clamp_min(1e-4) / 448)))
+    quant = (x / scale[:, None]).clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    return quant, scale
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mx_scales,three_axis", [(True, True), (False, False)])
+def test_pool_quantize_write(mx_scales, three_axis):
+    from vllm.models.hy_v4_flash.nvidia.indexpool_ops import pool_quantize_write
+
+    slots, ratio, page, blocks = 29, 4, 64, 64
+    # Values and gates are the two halves of one fused projection.
+    projection = torch.randn(slots, ratio, 256, device="cuda")
+    values, gates = projection[..., :128], projection[..., 128:]
+    ape = torch.randn(ratio, 128, device="cuda")
+    norm_weight = torch.rand(128, device="cuda") + 0.5
+    positions = torch.randint(
+        0, 50000, (3, slots) if three_axis else (slots,), device="cuda"
+    )
+    table = torch.randperm(blocks, device="cuda").int().reshape(4, 16)
+    owners = torch.randint(0, 4, (slots,), device="cuda").int()
+    groups = torch.arange(slots, device="cuda") * 7
+    active = torch.rand(slots, device="cuda") > 0.2
+
+    probabilities = (gates + ape).softmax(1)
+    pooled = F.rms_norm((values * probabilities).sum(1), (128,), norm_weight, 1e-5)
+    quant, scale = _fwht_quantize_reference(
+        _rotate_reference(pooled.bfloat16(), positions)
+    )
+    scale_bits = scale.view(torch.int32)
+    if mx_scales:
+        scale_bits = (scale_bits >> 23) * 0x01010101
+    expected = torch.zeros(blocks, page, 132, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    for slot in active.nonzero().flatten().tolist():
+        group = int(groups[slot])
+        block = int(table[owners[slot], group // page])
+        row = group % page
+        # A page holds `page` rows of 128 FP8 bytes, then `page` 4-byte scales.
+        flat = expected[block].view(-1)
+        flat[row * 128 : (row + 1) * 128] = quant[slot].view(torch.uint8)
+        flat[page * 128 :].view(torch.int32)[row] = scale_bits[slot]
+
+    cache = torch.zeros_like(expected)
+    pool_quantize_write(
+        projection,
+        ape,
+        norm_weight,
+        1e-5,
+        positions,
+        _ROPE,
+        cache,
+        table,
+        owners,
+        groups,
+        active,
+        mx_scales,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(cache, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+

+    try:
+        topk.resolve_backend(logits, min(budget, width), rows)
+    except RuntimeError as e:
+        pytest.skip(str(e))
+    logical = torch.randint(-1, width * ratio, (rows,), device="cuda")
+    # A row sees at most the width of its logits.
+    upper = (logical // ratio).clamp_min(0).int()
+    active = torch.rand(rows, device="cuda") > 0.1

+    columns = torch.arange(width, device="cuda")
+    scores = logits.masked_fill(columns[None] >= upper[:, None], -torch.inf)
+    values, indices = scores.topk(min(budget, width), dim=-1)
+    sentinel = torch.iinfo(torch.int32).max
+    groups = torch.where(values != -torch.inf, indices, sentinel).int().sort(-1).values
+    groups = F.pad(

+    live = (logical >= 0) & active
+    history = groups[..., None] * ratio + torch.arange(ratio, device="cuda")
+    valid = (groups >= 0) & (groups < upper[:, None]) & live[:, None]

+"""The CUDA iHC boundary must match the unfused post, pre and RMSNorm path."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils import (
+    per_token_group_quant_fp8_packed_for_deepgemm,

+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or not ops.hy_v4_ihc_boundary_supported(4, 6144),
+    reason="needs the CUDA hy_v4_ihc_boundary op",
+)
+
+HC, MAGNITUDE, HC_EPS, NORM_EPS, VARIANCE_EPS = 4, 2.0, 1e-6, 1e-5, 1e-5
+
+
+def _rms_norm(x, weight, eps):
+    """Match the CUDA rms_norm: one rounding of x * rsqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * w."""
+    xf = x.float()
+    scale = torch.rsqrt(xf.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    return (xf * scale * weight.float()).to(x.dtype)
+
+
+def _unfused(xa, residual, post, weight, scale, base, norm_weight):
+    if xa is not None:
+        residual = triton_ihc_post(xa, residual, post)
+    hidden, gates = triton_ihc_pre(
+        residual, weight, scale, base, MAGNITUDE, HC_EPS, NORM_EPS
+    )
+    if norm_weight is not None:
+        hidden = _rms_norm(hidden, norm_weight, VARIANCE_EPS)
+    return residual, hidden, gates
+
+
+def _fp32_reduction_reference(residual, weight, scale, base, norm_weight):
+    """Gated reduction kept in high precision into the norm (no BF16 rounding
+    before it), as round_before_norm=False and the HPC library compute."""
+    r = residual.double()
+    flat = r.flatten(1)
+    mixes = flat @ weight.double().t()
+    rstd = torch.rsqrt(flat.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + NORM_EPS)
+    pre = torch.sigmoid(mixes[:, :HC] * rstd * scale[0] + base[:HC]) + HC_EPS
+    hidden = (pre[:, :, None] * r).sum(1)
+    if norm_weight is not None:
+        hidden = hidden * torch.rsqrt(
+            hidden.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + VARIANCE_EPS
+        )
+        hidden = hidden * norm_weight.double()
+    return hidden.to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _inputs(num_tokens, hidden_size, offset_views):
+    torch.manual_seed(num_tokens)
+    device = "cuda"
+    # Offset views start one token in: still 16-byte aligned, but not at the
+    # allocation base.
+    pad = 1 if offset_views else 0
+    residual = (torch.randn(num_tokens + pad, HC, hidden_size, device=device) * 2).to(
+        torch.bfloat16
+    )[pad:]
+    xa = torch.randn(num_tokens + pad, hidden_size, device=device).to(torch.bfloat16)[
+        pad:
+    ]
+    post = torch.rand(num_tokens, HC, device=device) * 2
+    weight = torch.randn(2 * HC, HC * hidden_size, device=device) * 6e-3
+    scale = torch.tensor([0.5, 0.5], device=device)
+    base = torch.randn(2 * HC, device=device) * 0.5
+    norm_weight = (1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(hidden_size, device=device)).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    return xa, residual, post, weight, scale, base, norm_weight
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 8, 1024])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hidden_size", [3072, 6144])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_post", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_norm", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offset_views", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("round_before_norm", [False, True])
+def test_boundary_matches_reference(
+    num_tokens, hidden_size, with_post, with_norm, offset_views, round_before_norm
+):
+    _check_boundary(
+        num_tokens, hidden_size, with_post, with_norm, offset_views, round_before_norm
+    )
+
+
+def _check_boundary(
+    num_tokens,
+    hidden_size,
+    with_post,
+    with_norm,
+    offset_views,
+    round_before_norm,
+):
+    xa, residual, post, weight, scale, base, norm_weight = _inputs(
+        num_tokens, hidden_size, offset_views
+    )
+    if not with_post:
+        xa = post = None
+    if not with_norm:
+        norm_weight = None
+
+    new_residual, hidden, gates, _ = ops.hy_v4_ihc_boundary(
+        residual,
+        xa,
+        post,
+        weight,
+        scale,
+        base,
+        norm_weight,
+        MAGNITUDE,
+        HC_EPS,
+        NORM_EPS,
+        VARIANCE_EPS,
+        round_before_norm,
+    )
+
+    if with_post:
+        # The post step is one FMA: the exact result rounded to BF16, up to
+        # double rounding through FP32 (one BF16 step).
+        exact = post.double()[:, :, None] * xa.double()[:, None, :]
+        exact = exact + residual.double()
+        one_step = exact.to(torch.bfloat16).double().abs() * 2.0**-7
+        assert ((new_residual.double() - exact).abs() <= one_step).all()
+    else:
+        assert new_residual.data_ptr() == residual.data_ptr()
+    # From the same residual, gates and the reduced hidden state differ from
+    # the reference only by FP32 summation order: the unfused pre and RMSNorm
+    # when rounding before the norm, else a high-precision reduction.
+    _, ref_hidden, ref_gates = _unfused(
+        None, new_residual, None, weight, scale, base, norm_weight
+    )
+    if not round_before_norm:
+        ref_hidden = _fp32_reduction_reference(
+            new_residual, weight, scale, base, norm_weight
+        )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(gates, ref_gates, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4)
+    diff = (hidden.float() - ref_hidden.float()).abs()
+    rel_l2 = diff.norm() / ref_hidden.float().norm()
+    # One flipped BF16 rounding can dominate a one-token row on its own.
+    one_flip = (diff > 0).sum() <= 1 and (
+        diff <= ref_hidden.float().abs() * 2.0**-7
+    ).all()
+    assert rel_l2 < 2e-4 or one_flip, rel_l2

+"""Fused Triton kernels for the HY V4 Flash Engram layer."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["hashes_stride", "vocab_start", "vocab_end"])
+def _lookup_norm_kernel(
+    table_ptr,
+    scales_ptr,
+    hashes_ptr,
+    gamma_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    hashes_stride,
+    vocab_start,
+    vocab_end,
+    eps,
+    HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_SCALES: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    token = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    heads = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)[:, None]
+    lanes = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)[None, :]
+    head_mask = heads < HEADS
+    mask = head_mask & (lanes < DIM)
+
+    bucket = tl.load(
+        hashes_ptr + token * hashes_stride + heads, mask=head_mask, other=-1
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    found = head_mask & (bucket >= vocab_start) & (bucket < vocab_end)
+    row = tl.where(found, bucket - vocab_start, 0)
+    x = tl.load(table_ptr + row * DIM + lanes, mask=mask & found, other=0.0)
+    x = x.to(tl.float32)
+    if HAS_SCALES:
+        x *= tl.load(scales_ptr + row, mask=found, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    rstd = tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(x * x, axis=1) / DIM + eps)[:, None]
+    gamma = tl.load(gamma_ptr + heads * DIM + lanes, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + (token * HEADS + heads) * DIM + lanes,
+        (x * rstd * gamma.to(tl.float32)).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=mask,
+    )
+
+
+def lookup_norm(
+    table: torch.Tensor,
+    scales: torch.Tensor | None,
+    hashes: torch.Tensor,
+    vocab_start: int,
+    vocab_end: int,
+    gamma: torch.Tensor,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Gather, dequantize and RMS-normalize Engram table rows per head.
+
+    Args:
+        table: `[vocab_end - vocab_start, dim]` local table rows (FP8 or
+            BF16), possibly a CUDA view of pinned host memory.
+        scales: `[vocab_end - vocab_start]` FP8 row scales, or None for BF16
+            tables.
+        hashes: `[T, heads]` global buckets; a bucket outside
+            `[vocab_start, vocab_end)`, including a negative one, zeroes its
+            head.
+        vocab_start: First global bucket of `table`.
+        vocab_end: End of the global buckets of `table`.
+        gamma: `[heads, dim]` per-head norm weights.
+        dtype: output dtype.
+
+    Returns:
+        `[T, heads * dim]` normalized rows.
+
+    """
+    num_tokens, heads = hashes.shape
+    dim = table.shape[1]
+    assert table.is_contiguous() and gamma.shape == (heads, dim)
+    assert gamma.is_contiguous() and hashes.stride(1) == 1
+    out = torch.empty(num_tokens, heads * dim, dtype=dtype, device=hashes.device)
+    if num_tokens == 0 or heads == 0:
+        return out.zero_()

+        table if scales is None else scales,
+        hashes,
+        gamma,

+        hashes.stride(0),
+        vocab_start,
+        vocab_end,
+        torch.finfo(torch.float32).eps,

+        DIM=dim,
+        BLOCK_H=triton.next_power_of_2(heads),
+        BLOCK_D=triton.next_power_of_2(dim),
+        HAS_SCALES=scales is not None,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )

+    hidden_ptr,
+    proj_ptr,
+    hashes_ptr,
+    key_norm_ptr,
+    query_norm_ptr,
+    pre_gamma_ptr,
+    hc_scales_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    hidden_stride_t,
+    hidden_stride_h,
+    proj_stride,
+    hashes_stride,
+    out_stride_t,
+    out_stride_h,
+    num_hash_cols,
+    eps,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    HC_MULT: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_C: tl.constexpr,

+    program = tl.program_id(0)
+    token = (program // HC_MULT).to(tl.int64)

+        hidden_ptr + token * hidden_stride_t + channel * hidden_stride_h + lanes,

+    value = tl.load(proj + HC_MULT * DIM + lanes, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    key_norm = tl.load(key_norm_ptr + channel * DIM + lanes, mask=mask, other=0.0)
+    query_norm = tl.load(query_norm_ptr + channel * DIM + lanes, mask=mask, other=0.0)

+    # Round at the same tensor boundaries as the eager BF16 chain.
+    key = (key * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(key * key) / DIM + eps) * key_norm.to(tl.float32)).to(

+    normed_query = (
+        query * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(query * query) / DIM + eps) * query_norm.to(tl.float32)
+    ).to(dtype)

+    dot = (dot * (1.0 / tl.sqrt(float(DIM)))).to(dtype).to(tl.float32)

+    signal = pre_gamma * value * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(value * value) / DIM + eps)

+    update = ((gate + hc_scale.to(tl.float32)) * signal).to(dtype).to(tl.float32)

+    columns = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_C)
+    hashes = tl.load(
+        hashes_ptr + token * hashes_stride + columns,
+        mask=columns < num_hash_cols,
+        other=-1,
+    )
+    live = tl.max((hashes >= 0).to(tl.int32)) > 0

+        out_ptr + token * out_stride_t + channel * out_stride_h + lanes,
+        tl.where(live, query + update, query).to(dtype),
+        mask=mask,
+    )
